sections.h2: Which Osceola County office answers my tax question?
sections.html:
The work is split three ways, and each office has its own phone number, so choose before you dial. The Property Appraiser decides assessed value and takes care of exemptions, tangible property returns and the tax roll. Call (407) 742-5000, or use the website, which has a tax estimator and a homestead filing page. Notices, payments and the tax certificate process belong to the Tax Collector. Deeds and mortgages are filed with the clerk, who doubles as county recorder.

For the Tax Collector, dial 407-742-4000. Four offices keep weekday hours until 4:00 pm: the main office at 2501 E. Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy in Kissimmee, another at 2595 Simpson Road in Kissimmee, a St. Cloud office at 1300 9th Street, Suite 101B, and a Campbell City office at 4730 South Orange Blossom Trail. Appointments can be booked online.

  • Osceola County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, millage page, tax estimator.
  • Osceola County Tax Collector: notices, payment, installment plan, certificates.
  • Osceola Clerk of Court and Comptroller: Official Records search, which includes a property fraud alert signup.

Collection for the calendar-year assessment opens November 1. Notices usually reach the last address on the tax roll by that date. You can pay through March, and April 1 is the delinquency date.

Lenders that escrow your tax are expected to request the bill and send you a copy. The collector still treats it as your job to confirm the tax is paid and a bill was received.

Dates an Osceola County owner should know
DateWhat happens
January 1Assessment and valuation date
March 1Deadline to file for exemptions
March 31Gross amount due on real estate tax
April 1Unpaid real estate tax delinquent, 3 percent charge added; tangible personal property returns due
April 30Installment plan applications for next year due

NovemberCollection opens, top discount through November 30

sections.h2: Early discounts and the installment plan
sections.html:
A November payment cuts the bill by 4 percent. The reduction shrinks by a point every month until it is 1 percent in February, and a March payment is the gross amount.

Prefer four smaller payments? Apply for the installment plan by April 30 of the year before the bill, and make the first payment by June 30. A July payment gives up the discount and carries a 5 percent late charge; if July 31 passes with nothing paid, the plan is cancelled. Two more installments are due September 30 and December 31.

Furniture, fixtures and equipment used in a business or rental, along with structural additions to mobile homes, are taxed on a separate tangible personal property bill. When the estimate tops $100.00, quarterly payment is allowed. Landlords selling a furnished rental should ask the appraiser about the April 1 return.

  • Both kinds of bill qualify for the early payment discounts.
  • Changes to a name, an address or an assessed value are made at the Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector.

sections.h2: Homestead for a seller or buyer
sections.html:
The application deadline with the Property Appraiser is March 1, and the benefit begins in the year you file. State materials describe a ceiling of $50,000 in two tiers; only the first tier applies to school taxes.

The appraiser's website includes a File Homestead page and a form for reporting exemption fraud, while the clerk runs a separate property fraud alert. Tell the appraiser when you sell. A sale or deed ends the capped assessment, and value resets on the following January 1. The buyer files a fresh application by March 1 if the house will be a residence.

Farmland holds its own classification, and Osceola's appraiser says that classification does not pass to a new owner. Someone buying pasture or grove land applies again in the January to March window, and classified parcels are re-inspected at least every three years.

The steps run in a set order. April 1 adds a 3 percent charge to unpaid tax. Advertising comes next, then the sale of a lien, and two years later the certificate holder may apply for a tax deed.

A local newspaper prints the delinquent list, in parcel order, three weeks in a row. On or before June 1 the collector auctions certificates online through LienHub. Bids start at 18 percent, and the investor willing to take the lowest rate wins. What that investor holds is a lien, not a deed, and it carries no right to enter your property.

You clear it by paying the certificate amount, interest at the sold rate and, from June 1 onward, a $6.25 redemption fee. Certificates that drew no bidder are offered afterward on LienHub. A certificate still outstanding on the second April 1 after the sale lets its holder request a tax deed, once other certificates on the parcel and the present year's tax are paid.

  • A certificate holder is barred from demanding payment from you in the first two years.
  • A lien does not block a sale; the closing pays it off.

sections.h2: Taxes and the deed at closing
sections.html:
At closing the tax lien is paid off first, and the deed is then entered in the Official Records. Florida charges documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of price on the deed, apart from Miami-Dade, where the rate differs. All signers of the deed share liability, and the clerk collects the tax when the deed is recorded.

Page-by-page recording charges are set by statute, with a modernization trust fund charge and a technology charge on top. The clerk also has a branch office in Poinciana.

Timing counts. November is when bills go out, so a closing earlier in the year happens before the new bill exists. Ask the closing agent how the year will be prorated, and file the Tax Collector's payoff letter with your closing papers. If a 10 percent non-homestead cap applied to your rental, expect the buyer's value to reset after the sale.

sections.h2: What a seller can do this month
sections.html:
Pull up the parcel on the appraiser's site and confirm the owner name and any exemption are right. Then look at the Tax Collector's account for the same parcel and note which years are paid. If there is a balance, phone 407-742-4000 and ask for the payoff in writing. Finally, put the payoff letter, your latest notice and a copy of the deed into one folder for the title agent.

Choosing between a regular listing and a cash sale does not change any of this. The tax lien rides with the parcel either way, and closing pays it from the proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the delinquency date for Osceola County tax?
faqs.a: April 1. The Tax Collector adds a 3 percent charge to the gross amount that day, advertises the delinquent list, and runs an online lien auction by June 1.

faqs.q: What discounts does the Osceola County Tax Collector give?
faqs.a: Four percent off for November, then a point less each month through February. March brings no discount, and March 31 is the gross due date.

faqs.q: Where is the Osceola County Tax Collector?
faqs.a: The main office is at 2501 E. Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy in Kissimmee. Others sit on Simpson Road in Kissimmee, in St. Cloud and in Campbell City, all on the 407-742-4000 line.

faqs.q: How do I redeem an Osceola County tax certificate?
faqs.a: Pay the certificate amount plus interest at the rate it sold for, and a $6.25 fee when redeeming on or after June 1. Contact the Tax Collector for the exact payoff.

faqs.q: Does back tax stop me from selling in Osceola County?
faqs.a: No. The lien rides with the parcel and the payoff is deducted at closing. Before you sign, phone 407-742-4000 and ask the Tax Collector for the number.
